VIX.label: VIX
VIX.source: Polygon I:VIX daily bars, Friday's settle. CLOSED - Cboe does not compute VIX on a US market holiday. REJECTED INPUT, DISCLOSED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: Polygon served a daily bar dated 2026-09-07 for this ticker and for no other index, and this run refused it on three independent grounds. First, it MUTATED between two fetches minutes apart - initially close 15.14 with a high of 15.16, then open 15.02, high 15.17, low 14.99, close 15.17. A settled close does not move. Second, its close equalled its high exactly, the signature of a thin accumulating partial bar. Third, no sibling bar exists for I:SPX, I:NDX, I:SOX, I:DJI or I:VXN, and since VIX and VXN are both Cboe-calculated off the same session a VIX print without a VXN print is not possible. Shipping that figure would have invented a volatility move on a day the options market was shut. On the real number: VIX rose 1.467% Friday to 14.53 and is essentially unchanged on the week from 14.43. A payrolls print that repriced the September FOMC toward a HIKE moved implied volatility two tenths of a point. Companion VXN fell to 20.04 from 20.16.

WTI.label: WTI Crude
WTI.source: LIVE TILE. CLUSD front-month, print 92.26 timestamped 2026-09-07 11:08:29 UTC, against Friday's 91.48 settle - up 0.853% in a holiday-thinned session, with a Monday range of 90.88 to 93.03. CME energy ran holiday hours, so this is a real market, but it is a thin one and Reuters explicitly described light trade with Wall Street shut. Two developments inside the overnight window point the same way. OPEC+ paused its run of monthly output increases, holding October required production at September levels, which removes the supply-side offset that had been absorbing the Iran risk premium. And Kpler transit counts through Hormuz fell to a 10-day moving average of 10 commodity ships a day as of Sunday, the lowest since May, from above 15 on Friday, with only two vessels physically transiting Saturday and six Sunday. Throughput is collapsing while the group has stopped adding barrels. On the week WTI is up roughly 10%.

BRENT.label: Brent Crude
BRENT.source: LIVE TILE. BZUSD front-month, print 97.42 timestamped 2026-09-07 11:08:34 UTC, against Friday's 96.28 settle - up 1.184%, outpacing WTI and widening the Brent-WTI spread to $5.16 from $4.80. That widening is the informative part: the seaborne benchmark carries Strait of Hormuz risk more directly than the landlocked US grade, which is what you would expect given where the escalation is happening. Iran's SNSC secretary Mohsen Rezaei said Sunday that Tehran will declare an exclusion zone outside Hormuz within days and place any ship entering it on an Iranian sanctions list. Brent rose 7.8% last week. Vendor spread on this morning's level is worth noting rather than averaging: intraday prints between 96.9 and 97.6 were reported at different clock times, and 97.42 is this run's own timestamped read.

EURJPY.label: EUR/JPY
EURJPY.source: LIVE TILE. Print 179.81 timestamped 2026-09-07 11:08:32 UTC against a prior close of 181.46 - down 0.910%, and the day's range of 179.22 to 181.48 means the pair traded the whole distance from Friday's settle to a fresh low in one holiday session. This is the cleanest read on the carry complex and today it IS moving. The cause is identifiable and sits on the yen leg, not the euro leg: Takuji Aida, economic adviser to Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and a self-identified reflationist, said Monday that the Bank of Japan is likely to hike in September and to keep hiking once a quarter through January 2027, taking the policy rate to 1.25%. A dove inside the Prime Minister's own circle conceding the hike is a materially different signal from a hawkish economist predicting one. Note what did NOT move it: the AfD's win in Saxony-Anhalt left the euro steady, and Frankfurt's own desk wrote that the election played no role on the floor.

AUDJPY.label: AUD/JPY
AUDJPY.source: LIVE TILE. Print 111.65 timestamped 2026-09-07 11:04:42 UTC against a prior close of 112.54 - down 0.791%, with a range of 111.25 to 112.61. The classic risk-appetite carry proxy, and it answers the interpretive question this brief has been carrying for a week: is the yen's strength a disorderly carry unwind or an orderly repricing of Bank of Japan policy? Today's evidence says repricing, but less comfortably than Friday's did. The move is broad rather than pair-specific - USD/JPY fell 0.971% to 154.71 with a low of 154.05, a six-month low that broke the 155.15 support and tested the 24 February low, and daily RSI is around 27 - yet Asian equities RALLIED into it, with the Nikkei up 2.12% and the Kospi up 4.61%. A genuine carry unwind takes equities down with the pair. What you have instead is a yen repricing on a specific policy signal, in a thin holiday session, with the Bank of Japan meeting 17-18 September.
